title: The Truth About Crikvenica Prices and a 2027 Budget
metaDescription: Crikvenica is not the cheap Croatian coast it used to be. See 2026 price changes and a realistic 2027 daily budget for lodging, food, parking and transport.
content:
## Myth 1: Crikvenica is still the cheap corner of the Croatian coast

**The myth:** Kvarner towns cost far less than Split, Hvar or Dubrovnik, so prices stay low.

**The reality:** Crikvenica sits in the mid-range tier. It is cheaper than the best-known Dalmatian and island resorts, but not cheap in July and August. Apartments with a kitchen typically cost €60–150 per night depending on size and location. Basic guesthouse rooms run €40–90. Three-star hotels such as those in nearby Selce land around €85–180. Four-star Hotel Kvarner Palace reaches €180–350 in peak season. Prices fall sharply outside the summer weeks.

The tourist tax is also higher than many visitors expect. In 2026 Crikvenica charges €2.50 per adult per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.50 for the rest of the year. Ages 12 to 17 pay half, and children under 12 are exempt. A family of two adults staying seven nights in summer pays €35 in tax alone.

**Better alternative:** Book the last week of May, June or the first half of September. The same apartment often drops by a third or more, and the sea is warm enough for swimming through mid-September. Low-season rates for small apartments near the beach can sit near €80–100 a night in September, against much higher peak weeks.

## Myth 2: Apartments are always cheaper than hotels

**The myth:** A private apartment automatically beats a hotel on cost.

**The reality:** For two people, an apartment at €60–150 per night is often competitive only if breakfast and parking are not needed. Add the tourist tax, a cleaning fee and parking, and the gap with a €90–180 three-star hotel can shrink. Apartments clearly win for families of four or more and for stays of a week or longer, when a kitchen cuts food costs.

**Better alternative:** Filter for free on-site parking. Many Crikvenica apartments include it, and that matters, because central pay parking runs up to about €25 per day in the busiest zones. For stays under four nights, compare a hotel with breakfast against the full apartment cost before deciding.

**Insider perspective:** Properties in Dramalj, Selce and Jadranovo, a short bus or coastal-path ride from the center, usually price below equivalent places on the Crikvenica promenade. They cost less without losing much beach access.

## Myth 3: Eating out costs little because it is a regional town

**The myth:** Restaurant prices here are far below the Croatian coastal average.

**The reality:** Casual food is fair value. Pizza costs €10–15 and ćevapi €8–12. A main course at a sit-down restaurant on the waterfront usually costs €18–30, and a seafood platter for two €50–70. A mid-range three-course dinner for two lands near €50–55. A cheap meal at a basic eatery is about €11.

The seafood platter for two is usually not worth it. At €50–70 it costs roughly the same as two separate fish mains, and grilled whole fish sold by weight at a konoba gives more control over the bill. Ask for the price per kilogram before ordering.

**Better alternative:** Make lunch the main restaurant meal, buy breakfast and picnic items at a supermarket, and keep one proper seafood dinner per trip. A couple eating this way spends about €45–70 a day on food. A couple eating every meal at a restaurant spends €90–130.

## Myth 4: The beach is free, so a beach day costs nothing

**The myth:** Public beaches mean zero daily cost.

**The reality:** Entry to the town beach is free, but driving to it is not. Peak-season parking near the beach runs about €1.50–3.00 per hour, with central daily tickets up to roughly €25. Outer zones, a 10–15 minute walk away, cost about €1.00–1.50 per hour or €10–15 per day. Sunbed and activity costs add more: a jet ski runs €50–70 for 30 minutes, and Adrenalin Park costs about €20–35 per person.

**Better alternative:** Leave the car at the accommodation and walk the promenade. Use the local bus between Crikvenica, Selce, Dramalj and Jadranovo. A family that avoids central parking for a week saves €70–175.

## Myth 5: Day trips and transport need a big budget

**The myth:** Getting around the Kvarner coast requires a rental car and expensive tours.

**The reality:** Public transport is the cheapest category. The bus from Crikvenica to Rijeka costs €7.40 and takes about 40–45 minutes, with around a dozen departures a day. The passenger boat to Šilo on Krk takes 20–25 minutes and costs about €8.50 one way. The Zagreb–Crikvenica motorway toll is €8.90 for a car. Rijeka Airport, on Krk, is roughly a 26-minute drive from town. Organized boat trips to Krk cost €45–60 per adult, several times the independent ferry fare.

**Better alternative:** Take the Šilo boat and bus to Rijeka on your own. Rent a car only for one or two days if you want to reach remote parts of Krk or Cres.

**Insider perspective:** Crikvenica Aquarium (about €7–8 for adults) is one of the few paid attractions in town and works as a low-cost rainy-day option. It is a better use of money than a guided excursion on a day with bad weather.

## A realistic 2027 budget

These are forecasts built on 2026 price levels plus a modest 3–6% rise, which fits the recent trend of annual increases in Croatian tourism pricing. Treat them as planning ranges, not quotes. Figures are per couple per day, excluding flights.

| Style | June / September | July / August |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Budget (private room, self-catering, bus) | €85–120 | €120–170 |
| Mid-range (apartment, one restaurant meal a day) | €140–200 | €200–280 |
| Comfortable (4-star hotel, restaurants, boat trips) | €280–400 | €380–550+ |

For a week in an August mid-range setup, plan roughly €1,400–1,950 for two, including tourist tax and local transport. The same trip in the second week of September typically costs 25–35% less.

## What a first-time Crikvenica planner should lock in

Three decisions control most of the bill: the travel month, whether parking is included, and how many restaurant dinners are planned. Choose shoulder season, book an apartment with free parking in Selce or Dramalj if central rates are high, and use the bus and Šilo boat instead of paid excursions. Reserve early for July and August, because the best-value apartments disappear first. Add about €2.50 per adult per night for tourist tax to any quote that does not state it.

faq.question: But isn't Crikvenica much cheaper than Dubrovnik or Split?
faq.answer: It is cheaper, but the gap is smaller than the reputation suggests. Peak-season apartments cost €60–150 a night and restaurant mains €18–30. The savings come mainly from lodging and parking outside the main resort zones, and from visiting outside July and August.

faq.question: How much is the tourist tax in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: In 2026 it is €2.50 per adult per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.50 from October to March. Guests aged 12 to 17 pay half, and children under 12 are exempt. It is often collected at the property rather than included in the booking price.

faq.question: How much should I budget per day in Crikvenica in 2027?
faq.answer: A mid-range couple should plan about €140–200 per day in June and September and €200–280 in July and August. Budget travelers using private rooms and self-catering can manage €85–170. These are forecasts based on 2026 prices plus a modest increase.

faq.question: Is parking in Crikvenica expensive?
faq.answer: In peak season, central zones cost about €1.50–3.00 per hour and up to around €25 per day. Outer zones cost about €1.00–1.50 per hour. Many apartments include free parking, which is worth prioritizing in your search.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: No, not for most trips. The town and nearby Selce, Dramalj and Jadranovo are linked by local buses, and a bus to Rijeka costs €7.40. A car mainly helps for arrival from Zagreb, where the motorway toll is €8.90, or for day trips around Krk.

faq.question: What does a meal cost in Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Pizza costs €10–15, ćevapi €8–12 and a sit-down main course €18–30. A mid-range three-course dinner for two is around €50–55, and a seafood platter for two is €50–70. Eating the largest meal at lunch lowers the daily cost.

faq.question: When is the cheapest time to visit Crikvenica?
faq.answer: Outside the summer peak. Accommodation drops significantly in late May, June and September, and the tourist tax stays at the high-season €2.50 only until 30 September. From October the tax falls to €1.50, but many beach facilities reduce their hours.

quickAnswer: Many travelers still assume Crikvenica is a bargain alternative to Dalmatia that costs half as much. It no longer is. Peak-season apartments run €60–150 a night, a restaurant main costs €18–30, and the tourist tax is €2.50 per adult. A realistic 2027 budget is €100–140 per person per day in July and August.
